cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg35.txt <<'EOF'
fix(streams): the file:// unregistration guard tested the wrong bit, on both arches

`stream_wrapper_unregister("file")` reported success and changed nothing. The guard was there —
`__rt_fopen` loads the disabled-wrapper mask and refuses a plain path while `file://` is
unregistered — and it could never fire, because it tests BIT 0 under a comment asserting "Index 0
is `file` in the built-in wrapper list".

`file` is at index FIVE. Bit 0 is `https`. So the guard asked about a wrapper nobody had
unregistered, on both arches, and every open proceeded.

The x86 arm's own comment says why it exists: "without it here, `stream_wrapper_unregister("file")`
reported success on x86_64 and then changed nothing, so opens kept working". That is exactly the
state it was in — the fix was reintroduced as a bug by a hard-coded constant that stopped agreeing
with the table it was copied from.

The bit is now DERIVED from `STREAM_WRAPPERS` at emission time. A literal is a second copy of the
table's ordering and this one had already drifted; deriving it means reordering the table cannot
silently retarget the guard. The emitter also asserts the index still fits the 64-bit mask rather
than leaving a longer table to be discovered by a guard that quietly tests nothing.

MEASURED against `php -n` 8.5.6: after unregistering `file`, php refuses `fopen` on a bare path
and elephc now refuses it too; `stream_wrapper_restore("file")` brings both back.

STILL DIVERGENT, and this commit does not reach it: `file_get_contents`, `file_exists` and
`filesize` on a bare path keep working after the unregistration, because they enter through
`__rt_file_get_contents_maybe_phar`, `__rt_file_exists` and `__rt_filesize` rather than through
`__rt_fopen`, and only the opener carries the guard. php refuses all of them.
EOF
